recipes.name: Ribollita (Reboiled Italian Cabbage Soup)
ingredients_raw: 2 potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 bunch Swiss chard, trimmed and chopped
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
1.5 cups grated Parmesan cheese for topping

steps.text: Sort and rinse the beans before placing them in a large pot with the water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and cook 5 minutes. Turn off heat, cover, and let stand 1 1/2 hours. Drain.

Place the beans, chicken broth, garlic, sage leaves, bay leaves, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer until beans are tender, about 2 hours. Cool. Remove 1 cup of beans. Discard the bay leaves and sage leaves. Blend the remaining bean mixture with a hand mixer until smooth. Set aside.

Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions; cook and stir until transparent, about 10 minutes. Combine the carrots, celery, potatoes, cabbage, Swiss chard, and kale with the onions. Stir in the tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Cover, and cook until greens have wilted, stirring at least once, about 20 minutes. Stir in the pureed bean mixture, and cook 40 minute until the mixture thickens. Stir in the reserved beans. Adjust seasonings to taste. Add the toasted bread slices; cook until bread is soaked, about 10 minutes longer. Cool, and refrigerate overnight.
Reheat the soup over low heat until heated through, about 20 minutes. Serve each serving garnished with 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese and a drizzle of olive oil.

raw_recipe.headline: Ribollita (Reboiled Italian Cabbage Soup)
raw_recipe.description: Made in the classic Italian tradition, this hearty soup combines a white bean puree with a blend of vegetables including cabbage, kale, and Swiss chard, with toasted bread to thicken the mix. It's reheated ('ribollita') and served topped with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

review.reviewBody: Very filling soup! Similar to the one I had in Tuscany, minus the canned tomatoes which I left out as personal preference. Don't cook for too long or else the cabbage goes mushy and tasteless, and choose stale bread -soaked in cold water for a day or two- for the best results. A wonderful fall or winter soup that doesn't disappoint. Thanks for sharing Josie!

Our family had picked lots of produce at a farm and this was an excellent way to use it up. I cannot think of a kale and chard soup that I have enjoyed as much!

I bypassed the sauteing of veggies and just put them directly into the soup. We used Eden's canned cannellini beans instead of cooking from scratch and Muir Glen organic canned tomatoes. My french bread was a few days old. It was difficult to toast in my toaster, so I chose to fry it lightly with olive oil, and I would do that again, as it added lots of flavor! I also used a powdered vegetable broth from Frontier instead of chicken broth and a very small amount of diced jalapeno- not traditional but very tasty!

I had precooked beans in the freezer (canned would work too), so I skipped the first step. I only simmered the beans with seasonings for about half an hour while I prepped and cooked the rest of the veggies. When they were done and I added the stock, the consistency was perfect and I couldn't bring myself to add a loaf of bread (especially since the soup already filled my largest pot!). I stopped right there (did not simmer for 2 more hours), and instead filled individual bowls, put a piece of toast on top, topped with cheese (parm and cheddar), and put it under the broiler until bubbly, french onion soup style. Done this way it was delicious and only took me about an hour start to finish! Will probably make again with these changes.

I love this soup! The changes I've made is to add some hot Italian sausage while sauteing the onions, used canned cannellini beans instead of dried and will use whatever green I have on hand when I make it (kale, swiss chard, collard greens, etc). I tend to use more cabbage (at least 2 cups). I also omit the bread and reduce the amount of olive oil to just a TBS or 2 when sauteeing the onion and sausage. I have made this several times and it is always consistently good and a hit with whoever has it!

Following another reviewer's suggestion, I made it like french onion soup, with the bread on top and sprinkled with cheese, then melted in the broiler. That way, my gluten-free friends could enjoy it, too! I substituted spinach for the swiss chard. Delish!

First and foremost, I threw everything in a slow cooker (gasp!) excluding the greens. I also used canned beans (another gasp!). I let this simmer in a slow cooker for 8 hours and then added the greens the last 30 mins or so. I also added a stock that I had left over from a fish dish earlier in the week. Served over crusty day old bread and its was very feeling and comforting. I am sorry I did not prepare as directed, but I am sure it would be even better if I had. Thanks!

I made this soup with high hopes for it. I did change one thing, I did not put the bread in the soup. I'm only giving it three stars as this was a huge amount of work. There is no way 30 minutes is the prep time. I'm an experienced cook and found I was prepping forever. The instructions should advise the cook to prep everything prior to beginning any cooking. Good flavor, might make again but would cut the recipe in half.

Good soup. Made if for friends and they loved it. It makes a lot of soup so did half in my Crockpot. Cooked it on low for 2 hours and high for 3 1/2. Turned out great. Garlic, Sage and Bay Leaf were great spices. Use special olive oil from France as a special treat to finish each dish.

I've wanted to make this since seeing it featured on a Bravo cooking show (Around the World in 80 Plates). Well this week, my CSA box had just about all the ingredients, except the celery, garlic and onion (which I already had)! The only thing I did that was not per the recipe was to use canned beans (sorry, but I'm lazy that way), and I only had 1 can of cannellini beans, so I used garbanzos for the second can. Again, sorry! Aside from that, I followed the recipe, except to make a bigger batch so I can freeze the leftovers. This is a delicious soup, and I think it's a great way to serve super nutritious greens to the family! I love greens of all kinds, and can chase my boyfriend with them, but when I've made soups like white bean and Swiss chard, he enjoyed it. I work from home, so on my lunch break, I prepared the soup and left it simmering on the stove, as the prep work is fairly labor intensive (but well worth it). I had some already stale French bread, and I did cook some spicy chicken Italian sausage to add, for my boyfriend, as he always has to have meat with dinner. What I like about this soup is it can be made vegan/vegetarian by using a vegan chicken flavored broth (Superior Touch Better Than Bouillon), and meat/cheese eaters can add Parmesan (or sausage). I can easily serve this to my vegan and meat eating friends, knowing it's both delicious and hearty!

This is absolutely delicious and great for using a variety of greens from the garden. It looked like it made a ton, so I cut it down considerably, and I used canned cannellini beans. It's good even without the bread and cheese, but if you want a "comfort food," I suggest toasting a bit of rustic bread and sprinkling parmesan on the top and broiling it in the oven for a few minutes (like French onion soup, but bury the bread down in the soup so that it soaks up the deliciousness). It's delicious, warming, and comforting at the end of a twelve-hour shift. An excellent winter stew!

Absolutely delicious. Didn't have any Chard on hand, so I upped the cabbage a little bit. Also added a rind of Parmesan into the beans, but no changes other than that. My husband is NOT a soup eater, and he had 4 bowls of this soup. It's on our monthly rotation of meals now.
Very tasty

I've loved this soup forever. It was the soup my grandmother made all winter long. The vegetables changed depending on what was available. The one change I make is one I learned from her. She beat fresh eggs and soaked her stale bread in the eggs. She added this eggy mash to the soup. It was rich, filling and comforting.

We loved the soup recipe. It was amazing although it was amazing. It’s not nearly as amazing as your website. I’ve looked at a lot of them and you have covered all the answers. I’m very impressed. I don’t use any other site now but your thank you. Keep up the good work. Best wishes, SYLVIA Garratt.

I made this recipe tonight and the changes I made was to omit the tomatoes, sub canned white beans for the dried beans and I also omitted the bread because I plan on eating this for the next week and I did not think the bread would taste good after sitting in the soup. I added red pepper flakes to the recipe because I put that in everything I cook! It's a delicious, hearty, (healthy) comfort food.

I love this soup! It is so customizable! I have made it before without potatoes and with bacon or pancetta. I usually leave out putting the bread IN the soup; I serve it along side the soup. Definitely lots of veggies and greens. I make a big pot and freeze a large batch, since you do spend a lot of time cutting up the veggies.
Loved it, I added butternut squash to it, I had a medium cabbage and I added the whole thing,, it was wonderful. And an added bonus, no meat. Will be making this often, thanks for a great recipe!!
This was great!

Made this for Thanksgiving dinner - it was the first time people asked to take soup home! Labor intensive, but it was wonderful just to take the pot out of the fridge on turkey day and heat it up. I didn't make it with the bread and I did find that the parmesan cheese did give it the added flavor I liked. I used the canned beans as other suggested. Might try this again - with the bread next time! Was very good!
will make again. Used chic peas, didn't have the beans, used collard greens didn't have kale, used fresh garden tomatoes, didn't put bread in soup.
